source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS02 is a single 114 MW campus that accounts for 7.1 percent of Virginia's published data center capacity, third among the 25 state facilities that disclose megawatt figures.

That ranking rests on a narrow base. Virginia maps 330 data centers but only 25 publish an IT capacity figure, and those 25 sum to 1,603 MW. The state total is therefore a floor, not a measurement, and one campus holding 7.1 percent of it shows how much of the disclosed load sits in a handful of buildings. The 685,000 square feet of technical space at this site is the physical footprint behind that number.

For AI specifically, 114 MW is the unit that matters, because accelerator fleets are sized by the power and cooling a building can deliver rather than by chip count alone. The conversion to roughly 285 racks or about 2,280 high-end accelerators depends on stated assumptions of 400 watts per rack and 8 GPUs per rack, which are modeling choices and not observed configurations. The site sits in Sterling, 3.5 miles from Dulles, inside the Northern Virginia cluster where transmission and network routes already exist, so its capacity can be absorbed without new geography.

What the data does not cover is the constraint that would decide whether this capacity is usable. There is no figure for available versus contracted load, no power source, no interconnection status, and no grid or permitting limit on further expansion in Virginia. LEED certification describes how the building is managed, not where its electricity comes from. A 114 MW nameplate says what the campus can hold, not what it is running.
